title: The strict Roos cone preserves compatible homotopies
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with countable products [def-sp-abelian]. For a strict tower complex $X$ [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $P_X=\prod_nX_n$ termwise, $v_X=1-s_X$ with $\operatorname{pr}_ns_X=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$, and $\mathscr R(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(v_X)[-1]$ with coordinates $\mathscr R(X)^i=P_X^{i-1}\oplus P_X^i$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-v_Xx,dx)$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Sending a strict tower map $f$ to the diagonal map $(\prod_nf_n,\prod_nf_n)$ is additive and functorial. If strict tower maps $f,g:X\to Y$ have levelwise homotopies $h_n$ with $f_n-g_n=dh_n+h_nd$ and $t^Y_nh_{n+1}=h_nt^X_n$, they induce a homotopy from $\mathscr R(f)$ to $\mathscr R(g)$ with formula $(y,x)\mapsto(-h_Py,h_Px)$, where $h_P=\prod_nh_n$. Consequently $\mathscr R$ gives an additive functor $K(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to K(\mathcal A)$. If $\mathcal A$ is $k$-linear for a commutative ring $k$ [def-weil-linear-category], both the cochain and homotopy functors preserve multiplication of maps by $k$.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit); explicit homotopy calculation for the strict model, not asserted for arbitrary choices of derived limits.

proof.text: Use the termwise products and signed coordinates of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Write $\pi_{X,n}^i:P_X^i\to X_n^i$. For any degreewise family $a_n:X_n^i\to Y_n^j$, its product map $a_P:P_X^i\to P_Y^j$ is, by the universal property of products [def-weil-category-product], the unique map with $\pi_{Y,n}^ja_P=a_n\pi_{X,n}^i$. Therefore equality of maps into $P_Y^j$ can be checked after every projection. In particular products of maps preserve identities, composition and addition: the projections of $(ba)_P$ and $b_Pa_P$ are both $b_na_n\pi_{X,n}$, and those of $(a+b)_P$ and $a_P+b_P$ are both $(a_n+b_n)\pi_{X,n}$. These are identities of morphisms; coordinate notation below denotes biproduct components, not elements of arbitrary objects.

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), explicit product universal-property calculation for the strict model

proof.text: For a strict tower chain map $f$, set $F^i=(f_n^i)_P$. The chain-map and strictness equations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system] give $d_Y^iF^i=F^{i+1}d_X^i$ and $s_Y^iF^i=F^is_X^i$: the nth projection of the second equation is $t_{Y,n}^if_{n+1}^i\pi_{X,n+1}^i=f_n^it_{X,n}^i\pi_{X,n+1}^i$. Subtracting from $F^i$ gives $v_Y^iF^i=F^iv_X^i$. Consequently $D_Y^i\operatorname{diag}(F^{i-1},F^i)=\operatorname{diag}(F^i,F^{i+1})D_X^i$, since their respective components are $-d_YF y-v_YF x=F(-d_Xy-v_Xx)$ and $d_YF x=Fd_Xx$. Thus the prescribed diagonal map really is a cochain map.

proof.text: On both diagonal blocks the product identities from Step 1 give $\mathscr R(1_X)=1_{\mathscr R(X)}$, $\mathscr R(bf)=\mathscr R(b)\mathscr R(f)$ and $\mathscr R(f+g)=\mathscr R(f)+\mathscr R(g)$. Equality of the two biproduct components proves each equality of cochain maps. Also $\mathscr R(0)=0$. This proves the additive cochain functor asserted in the statement, with exactly the map prescription of [def-weil-strict-roos-model].

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), direct verification of the strict diagonal functor

proof.text: For the given compatible homotopy set $H^i=(h_n^i)_P:P_X^i\to P_Y^{i-1}$. Taking nth projections of $F^i-G^i$ and $d_Y^{i-1}H^i+H^{i+1}d_X^i$ gives respectively $(f_n^i-g_n^i)\pi_{X,n}^i$ and $(d_{Y,n}^{i-1}h_n^i+h_n^{i+1}d_{X,n}^i)\pi_{X,n}^i$, so these maps agree. Likewise the projections of $s_Y^{i-1}H^i$ and $H^is_X^i$ agree by $t_{Y,n}^{i-1}h_{n+1}^i=h_n^it_{X,n}^i$. Hence $v_Y^{i-1}H^i=H^iv_X^i$. Only existence of the products has been used, not exactness of products.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), direct product homotopy calculation; homology.tex, cochain homotopy definition before Tag 0112

proof.text: Define $T^i:\mathscr R(X)^i\to\mathscr R(Y)^{i-1}$ by $T^i(y,x)=(-H^{i-1}y,H^ix)$. With the differential of [def-weil-strict-roos-model], the two components of $D_Y^{i-1}T^i+T^{i+1}D_X^i$ are $((d_Y^{i-2}H^{i-1}+H^id_X^{i-1})y+(H^iv_X^i-v_Y^{i-1}H^i)x,\ (d_Y^{i-1}H^i+H^{i+1}d_X^i)x)$. The mixed term is zero by Step 4. The remaining diagonal blocks are $F^{i-1}-G^{i-1}$ and $F^i-G^i$, again by Step 4. Thus $D_YT+TD_X=\mathscr R(f)-\mathscr R(g)$, which is the required homotopy with the stated signs and degrees.

Here $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ has the strict maps of [def-weil-inverse-system], with sums and composition levelwise. A degree $-1$ map between its complexes is exactly a family $h_n^i$ commuting with transitions; commuting with adjacent transitions implies commuting with every transition by repeated composition. Thus the homotopies in $K(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ are exactly the compatible homotopies treated above. Explicitly $K$ has complexes as objects and chain maps modulo $f-g=dh+hd$. The homotopy relation is an equivalence relation: use $0,-h,h+h^{\prime}$ for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. It respects addition, since homotopies add. It respects composition, since for chain maps $a,b$ the equation $b(f-g)a=d(bha)+(bha)d$ follows by commuting $a,b$ past the differentials. All these operations preserve transition compatibility when performed in towers.

source.place: Tag 013H (definition-complexes-notation); elementary verification of the quotient operations of Tag 0112 (homology-lemma-compose-homotopy-cochain)

proof.text: Define the functor on homotopy categories by $X\mapsto\mathscr R(X)$ and $[f]\mapsto[\mathscr R(f)]$. Steps 4 and 5 make the map on classes independent of the representative. Step 3 gives preservation of identities, composition, addition and zero after taking classes, with the operations of Step 6. Thus the resulting functor $K(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to K(\mathcal A)$ is additive. No assertion about cones of arbitrary morphisms in a triangulated category is used: the construction uses the fixed strict cone of [def-weil-strict-roos-model].

Assume the $k$-linearity of [def-weil-linear-category]. For $c\in k$, $\pi_{Y,n}(cF)=c(\pi_{Y,n}F)=cf_n\pi_{X,n}$, so uniqueness of the product map [def-weil-category-product] gives $(cf)_P=cF$. Composing with biproduct projections similarly gives $\mathscr R(cf)=c\mathscr R(f)$. The module structure on chain maps is componentwise; the chain-map equations are stable under scalars by bilinearity of composition. If $f-g=dh+hd$, then $cf-cg=d(ch)+(ch)d$, and $ch$ is transition-compatible whenever $h$ is. Thus scalar multiplication is well-defined on both homotopy quotients, and $[\mathscr R(cf)]=c[\mathscr R(f)]$. Together with Step 3 this proves $k$-linearity of both functors.
